meaning.en: A public bar or drinking place, especially one associated with the American Old West.

meaning.en: A car with a separate boot/trunk; British English.

meaning.en: A plant or part of a plant that is eaten as food.

meaning.en: Not especially interesting, unusual or worthy of attention.

meaning.en: Not attractive, pleasant or interesting.

meaning.es: emotividad que provoca tristeza o compasión

meaning.en: Containing both happiness and sadness at the same time.

meaning.en: A small round red or dark fruit with a stone in the middle.

meaning.en: To a small degree; a little.

meaning.en: A flat shoe shaped like a ballet slipper.
example.en: She wore black ballerina flats with a simple summer dress.
example.es: Llevaba unas bailarinas negras con un vestido sencillo de verano.
notes: Footwear sense. The usual English term is “ballerina flat” (often plural “ballerina flats”); “ballerina” alone primarily means a ballet dancer. Original source term preserved.

meaning.en: A wild South American animal related to the llama.
example.en: We saw a guanaco grazing near the road.
example.es: Vimos un guanaco pastando cerca de la carretera.

meaning.en: To move around freely without a fixed direction or destination.
example.en: The animal roams freely across the reserve.
example.es: El animal deambula libremente por la reserva.
notes: Headword normalised from “roams” to lemma “roam”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: An occasion when something, especially something unusual, is seen.
example.en: The rare-bird sighting attracted dozens of visitors.
example.es: El avistamiento del ave rara atrajo a decenas de visitantes.

meaning.en: A large natural area with little or no human development.
example.en: They spent several days hiking through the wilderness.
example.es: Pasaron varios días caminando por una zona salvaje.

meaning.en: A thin piece of wood, especially one that has fallen or been cut from a tree.
example.en: He picked up a stick and threw it for the dog.
example.es: Cogió un palo y se lo lanzó al perro.

meaning.en: To become or make something fixed to a surface, often with glue.
example.en: Use tape to stick the label to the box.
example.es: Usa cinta adhesiva para pegar la etiqueta a la caja.

meaning.en: Large, satisfying and nourishing, especially when describing food.
example.en: We had a hearty meal after the long hike.
example.es: Tomamos una comida abundante después de la larga caminata.
notes: Food sense.

meaning.en: Warm, enthusiastic and sincere.
example.en: They gave us a hearty welcome when we arrived.
example.es: Nos dieron una bienvenida muy cordial cuando llegamos.
notes: Warm/enthusiastic sense.

meaning.en: To move very fast, often in a forceful or uncontrolled way.
example.en: The car hurtled down the hill at frightening speed.
example.es: El coche bajó la colina a una velocidad aterradora.
notes: Headword normalised from “hurtled” to lemma “hurtle”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: Not made, prepared or arranged; for example, an unmade bed.
example.en: His bed was still unmade at noon.
example.es: Su cama seguía sin hacer al mediodía.

meaning.en: Extremely fast and dangerous.
example.en: They drove along the narrow road at breakneck speed.
example.es: Condujeron por la carretera estrecha a una velocidad vertiginosa.

meaning.en: Pale, whitish or slightly cloudy in appearance.
example.en: The lake looked milky under the grey sky.
example.es: El lago parecía blanquecino bajo el cielo gris.

meaning.en: Extremely happy, excited and full of energy.
example.en: I felt exhilarated after reaching the summit.
example.es: Me sentí eufórica después de llegar a la cima.

meaning.en: Completely; used to emphasise an adjective or adverb.
example.en: The idea is utterly unrealistic.
example.es: La idea es totalmente irrealista.

meaning.en: The speed at which something happens or someone moves.
example.en: We walked at a steady pace for two hours.
example.es: Caminamos a un ritmo constante durante dos horas.

meaning.es: caminar de un lado a otro
meaning.en: To walk repeatedly backwards and forwards, especially because you are worried or impatient.
example.en: He paced up and down outside the interview room.
example.es: Caminaba de un lado a otro fuera de la sala de entrevistas.

meaning.en: To collect someone or something, often in a vehicle.
example.en: I'll pick you up at the station at six.
example.es: Te recogeré en la estación a las seis.

meaning.en: To learn or acquire a skill, language or habit without formal study.
example.en: She picked up a lot of English by watching series without subtitles.
example.es: Aprendió mucho inglés viendo series sin subtítulos.

meaning.en: In a regular, gradual and controlled way.
example.en: Sales have increased steadily since January.
example.es: Las ventas han aumentado de forma constante desde enero.

meaning.en: To approach a person or place by walking towards them.
example.en: A man walked up to us and asked for directions.
example.es: Un hombre se acercó caminando y nos pidió indicaciones.

meaning.en: To eat grass or other plants growing in a field.
example.en: Several sheep were grazing in the field.
example.es: Varias ovejas estaban pastando en el campo.
notes: Headword normalised from “grazing” to lemma “graze”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: A high or open place from which you can see a wide area.
example.en: We stopped at a lookout point to admire the valley.
example.es: Paramos en un mirador para contemplar el valle.

meaning.en: A group of animals of the same kind that live, feed or move together.
example.en: Large herds of deer move through the area in winter.
example.es: Grandes manadas de ciervos atraviesan la zona en invierno.
notes: Headword normalised from “herds” to lemma “herd”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: A roof made from sheets with a regular wavy or ridged surface.
example.en: Many of the old houses have corrugated roofs.
example.es: Muchas de las casas antiguas tienen tejados de chapa ondulada.
notes: Headword normalised from “corrugated roofs” to lemma “corrugated roof”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: A brief or incomplete view of something.
example.en: I caught a glimpse of the sea between the buildings.
example.es: Alcancé a ver fugazmente el mar entre los edificios.

meaning.en: To be important or have significance.
example.en: In the end, what mattered most was being together.
example.es: Al final, lo que más importó fue estar juntos.
relations.patterns: matter to someone; it doesn't matter
notes: Headword normalised from “mattered” to lemma “matter”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: A steep, rough mass of rock, especially on a mountain or cliff.
example.en: A lone climber stood on the edge of the crag.
example.es: Un escalador solitario estaba al borde del risco.

meaning.en: A low woody plant with many branches growing from near the ground.
example.en: A small bird was hiding in the bush.
example.es: Un pájaro pequeño se escondía en el arbusto.
notes: Plant sense.

meaning.en: Wild or uncultivated land covered with bushes and other vegetation.
example.en: The track disappeared into thick bush.
example.es: El sendero desaparecía entre el denso matorral.
notes: Wild-land sense.

meaning.en: A very large rounded or irregular rock.
example.en: A huge boulder blocked the path.
example.es: Una roca enorme bloqueaba el camino.

meaning.en: Extremely large in area, amount or size.
example.en: The desert stretches across a vast area.
example.es: El desierto se extiende por una zona enorme.

meaning.en: Impossible to know or fully understand.
example.en: Some aspects of the future are simply unknowable.
example.es: Algunos aspectos del futuro son sencillamente imposibles de conocer.

meaning.en: The activities, ideas and processes involved in governing a country or organisation.
example.en: She has always been interested in local politics.
example.es: Siempre le ha interesado la política local.

meaning.en: A hard transparent material used for windows, containers and many other objects.
example.en: The table is made of glass.
example.es: La mesa es de cristal.

meaning.en: The state of being free from unwanted attention or observation by other people.
example.en: The curtains give us more privacy from the neighbours.
example.es: Las cortinas nos dan más intimidad frente a los vecinos.

meaning.es: texto con huecos; ejercicio de completar huecos
meaning.en: A text with words removed that a learner has to complete.
example.en: In a cloze exercise, you have to fill in the missing words.
example.es: En un ejercicio de completar huecos, tienes que escribir las palabras que faltan.

meaning.en: A speech sound such as /a/, /e/, /i/, /o/ or /u/; also a letter representing one.
example.en: The letter “a” is a vowel.
example.es: La letra «a» es una vocal.

meaning.en: A common green plant with narrow leaves that grows on lawns and fields.
example.en: The grass was still wet from the rain.
example.es: La hierba seguía mojada por la lluvia.

meaning.en: An area of short, regularly cut grass, especially around a house.
example.en: They were sitting on the lawn in front of the house.
example.es: Estaban sentados en el césped delante de la casa.

meaning.en: A machine used for cutting grass on a lawn.
example.en: The lawn mower is in the shed.
example.es: El cortacésped está en el cobertizo.

meaning.en: A hard decorative stone used in buildings and sculpture.
example.en: The floor in the entrance hall is made of marble.
example.es: El suelo del vestíbulo es de mármol.
notes: Stone/material sense.

meaning.en: A small coloured glass ball used in children's games.
example.en: The child rolled a marble across the floor.
example.es: El niño hizo rodar una canica por el suelo.
notes: Toy sense.

meaning.en: The entrance area just inside the front door of a house or building.
example.en: Leave your coat in the hall by the front door.
example.es: Deja el abrigo en el vestíbulo junto a la puerta principal.
notes: Entrance-area sense.

meaning.en: A passage inside a building with doors leading to rooms.
example.en: Her office is at the end of the hall.
example.es: Su oficina está al final del pasillo.
notes: Passage/corridor sense.

meaning.en: A large entrance or waiting area in a hotel, office or public building.
example.en: We waited for them in the hotel lobby.
example.es: Los esperamos en el vestíbulo del hotel.

meaning.en: To tolerate or endure something difficult or unpleasant.
example.en: I can't bear the noise any longer.
example.es: Ya no aguanto más el ruido.

meaning.en: To consider a fact or circumstance when making a decision or judgement.
example.en: You should take the cost into account before making a decision.
example.es: Deberías tener en cuenta el coste antes de tomar una decisión.
notes: Normalised from source term: take into

meaning.en: A small house, especially in the countryside.
example.en: They rented a small cottage in the countryside.
example.es: Alquilaron una pequeña casa de campo.

meaning.en: The area near or around a particular place.
example.en: There are several good restaurants in the vicinity of the hotel.
example.es: Hay varios buenos restaurantes en los alrededores del hotel.

meaning.en: A roof covered with dried plant material such as straw or reeds.
example.en: The cottage has a traditional thatched roof.
example.es: La casita tiene un tejado de paja tradicional.
notes: Normalised from source term: tatched roof

meaning.en: The hot gas produced when water boils.
example.en: Steam rose from the cup of tea.
example.es: Salía vapor de la taza de té.

meaning.en: Having warm feelings for someone or liking something very much.
example.en: I'm very fond of walking by the sea.
example.es: Me gusta mucho caminar junto al mar.

meaning.en: A small shellfish with a dark shell that is commonly eaten.
example.en: We ordered mussels as a starter.
example.es: Pedimos mejillones de entrante.
notes: Headword normalised from “mussels” to lemma “mussel”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: The process of leaving one home and moving to another; especially common in British English.
example.en: Moving house can be stressful, even when everything is well organised.
example.es: Mudarse de casa puede ser estresante, incluso cuando todo está bien organizado.

meaning.en: Warm, comfortable and pleasant, especially a small place.
example.en: The living room is small but very cosy.
example.es: El salón es pequeño pero muy acogedor.

meaning.en: A period during which a person does not eat, usually for religious or health reasons.
example.en: He completed a twenty-four-hour fast.
example.es: Hizo un ayuno de veinticuatro horas.

meaning.en: To eat no food for a period of time, usually for religious or health reasons.
example.en: Some people fast for religious reasons.
example.es: Algunas personas ayunan por motivos religiosos.

meaning.en: An area or amount of room available for something.
example.en: There isn't enough space for another desk.
example.es: No hay suficiente espacio para otro escritorio.

meaning.en: Enough free space for someone or something.
example.en: Is there room for one more person in the car?
example.es: ¿Hay sitio para una persona más en el coche?
relations.confusedWith: space; room = a part of a building (another sense)
notes: Available-space sense.

meaning.en: A part of a building enclosed by walls, a floor and a ceiling.
example.en: The room has two large windows.
example.es: La habitación tiene dos ventanas grandes.
notes: Part-of-a-building sense.

meaning.en: A large strong box with a lid, used for storing things.
example.en: The old letters were kept in a wooden chest.
example.es: Las cartas antiguas se guardaban en un cofre de madera.

meaning.en: A sliding box-shaped storage compartment in a piece of furniture.
example.en: I found the keys in the top drawer.
example.es: Encontré las llaves en el cajón de arriba.

meaning.en: A piece of furniture with several drawers, used for storing clothes or other items.
example.en: Her clothes are stored in a chest of drawers.
example.es: Su ropa está guardada en una cómoda.

meaning.en: A small piece of material placed on a floor or other surface.
example.en: Put a mat by the door so people can wipe their shoes.
example.es: Pon una alfombrilla junto a la puerta para que la gente pueda limpiarse los zapatos.
notes: Source appears to contain a typo: 'mattered' → 'mat' based on the hint 'colchoneta'.

meaning.en: To satisfy or relieve your thirst by drinking.
example.en: A cold glass of water finally quenched my thirst.
example.es: Un vaso de agua fría por fin me sació la sed.
notes: Normalised from the source phrase “quench my thirst”.

meaning.en: A seat hanging from ropes or chains that moves backwards and forwards.
example.en: The children were playing on the swings in the park.
example.es: Los niños estaban jugando en los columpios del parque.
notes: Playground-seat sense.

meaning.en: A movement backwards and forwards or from side to side.
example.en: The slow swing of the lamp made the shadows move.
example.es: El lento balanceo de la lámpara hacía que las sombras se movieran.
notes: Movement sense.

meaning.en: To move backwards and forwards or from side to side.
example.en: The lamp began to swing from side to side.
example.es: La lámpara empezó a balancearse de un lado a otro.

meaning.en: Feeling angry or bitter because you believe you have been treated unfairly.
example.en: She felt resentful about being left out of the decision.
example.es: Se sentía resentida por haber quedado fuera de la decisión.
notes: Normalised from source term: resentfull

meaning.es: contracción informal/no estándar de am not/isn't/aren't/hasn't/haven't
meaning.en: A very informal, non-standard contraction used for am not, is not, are not, has not or have not.
example.en: “Ain't” is common in informal speech but is not standard in formal English.
example.es: «Ain't» es frecuente en el habla informal, pero no es estándar en el inglés formal.
notes: Normalised from source term: ain´t

meaning.en: A small flat in which the main living room, bedroom and kitchen are usually combined.
example.en: She rents a small studio flat near the university.
example.es: Alquila un pequeño estudio cerca de la universidad.

meaning.en: Having plenty of space inside.
example.en: The car is surprisingly roomy for such a small model.
example.es: El coche es sorprendentemente espacioso para ser un modelo tan pequeño.

meaning.en: Ready or happy to do something.
example.en: I'm willing to help if you need me.
example.es: Estoy dispuesto a ayudar si me necesitas.

meaning.es: pasillo (en avión, tren, teatro o supermercado)
meaning.en: A passage between rows of seats or shelves, for example on a plane or in a supermarket.
example.en: Would you prefer a window seat or an aisle seat?
example.es: ¿Prefieres un asiento de ventanilla o de pasillo?

meaning.en: A large indoor shopping complex; especially common in American English.
example.en: They spent the afternoon at a huge shopping mall outside the city.
example.es: Pasaron la tarde en un enorme centro comercial a las afueras de la ciudad.

meaning.en: A group or complex of shops; the usual British English term.
example.en: There's a new shopping centre near the station.
example.es: Hay un nuevo centro comercial cerca de la estación.

meaning.en: Old or ageing; often used politely about older people, though 'older' is often preferred.
example.en: The programme offers support for elderly people who live alone.
example.es: El programa ofrece apoyo a personas mayores que viven solas.

meaning.en: A purple vegetable with soft flesh; the British English word for eggplant.
example.en: In Britain, this vegetable is usually called an aubergine.
example.es: En Gran Bretaña, esta verdura suele llamarse «aubergine».
notes: Normalised from source term: albergine

meaning.en: A purple vegetable with soft flesh; the American English word for aubergine.
example.en: In American English, an aubergine is called an eggplant.
example.es: En inglés americano, una berenjena se llama «eggplant».

meaning.en: A long green vegetable; the British English word for zucchini.
example.en: We added sliced courgette to the pasta sauce.
example.es: Añadimos calabacín en rodajas a la salsa de pasta.

meaning.en: A long green vegetable; the American English word for courgette.
example.en: Zucchini is the usual American English word for courgette.
example.es: «Zucchini» es la palabra habitual en inglés americano para «courgette».

meaning.en: To move or run away suddenly and very quickly.
example.en: The horse suddenly bolted when it heard the noise.
example.es: El caballo salió disparado al oír el ruido.

meaning.en: A metal fastener, usually used with a nut, for joining things together.
example.en: Tighten the bolt with a suitable nut.
example.es: Aprieta el perno con una tuerca adecuada.
notes: Duplicate term retained as a separate source row for review.

meaning.en: A small metal piece with a threaded hole that screws onto a bolt.
example.en: The bolt is secured with a metal nut.
example.es: El perno está sujeto con una tuerca metálica.
notes: Metal-fastener sense.

meaning.en: A dry fruit or seed with a hard shell that can be eaten.
example.en: Nuts are a useful source of healthy fats.
example.es: Los frutos secos son una buena fuente de grasas saludables.
notes: Food sense.

meaning.en: A metal fastener with a spiral thread, turned to hold things together.
example.en: Use a screwdriver to tighten the screw.
example.es: Usa un destornillador para apretar el tornillo.

meaning.en: Showing good judgement and practical thinking.
example.en: It would be sensible to check the weather before leaving.
example.es: Sería sensato comprobar el tiempo antes de salir.

meaning.en: Easily affected emotionally or physically; aware of other people's feelings.
example.en: She's very sensitive to criticism.
example.es: Es muy sensible a las críticas.
notes: False-friend correction suggested: Spanish 'sensible' normally maps to English 'sensitive'.

meaning.en: A person whose job is to help customers and sell goods in a shop.
example.en: The shop assistant helped me find the right size.
example.es: La dependienta me ayudó a encontrar la talla correcta.
notes: Normalised from “shop assistant/employee” to a single headword.

meaning.en: A sudden flash or discharge of lightning.
example.en: A bolt of lightning struck a tree near the house.
example.es: Un rayo cayó sobre un árbol cerca de la casa.

meaning.en: To clean a floor or surface using a brush or broom.
example.en: Could you sweep the kitchen floor, please?
example.es: ¿Puedes barrer el suelo de la cocina, por favor?

meaning.en: To make someone or something completely wet.
example.en: The heavy rain soaked our clothes within minutes.
example.es: La lluvia intensa empapó nuestra ropa en cuestión de minutos.
notes: Make-completely-wet sense.

meaning.en: To leave something in liquid for a period of time so that it becomes soft, clean or absorbs the liquid.
example.en: Soak the beans in water overnight.
example.es: Deja las judías en remojo toda la noche.
relations.patterns: soak something in + liquid; soak for + period
notes: Leave-in-liquid sense.

meaning.en: A building where films are shown; the usual American English term.
example.en: We went to the movie theater to see the new release.
example.es: Fuimos al cine a ver el nuevo estreno.

meaning.es: cine (inglés británico; también común en otros dialectos)
meaning.en: A building where films are shown; the usual British English term.
example.en: Let's go to the cinema this weekend.
example.es: Vamos al cine este fin de semana.

meaning.en: Used to show accompaniment, possession, an instrument, a characteristic or a relationship.
example.en: She went to the concert with her sister.
example.es: Fue al concierto con su hermana.

meaning.es: dentro de; en el interior de
meaning.en: Inside the limits or boundaries of a place, area or range.
example.en: The village lies within the national park.
example.es: El pueblo se encuentra dentro del parque nacional.
notes: Space/boundary sense.

meaning.es: dentro de; en un plazo de
meaning.en: Before the end of a stated period of time.
example.en: Please reply within five working days.
example.es: Por favor, responde en un plazo de cinco días laborables.
notes: Time-limit sense.

meaning.en: A yellow spice made from the root of a plant, often used in curries.
example.en: Turmeric gives the curry a warm yellow colour.
example.es: La cúrcuma le da al curry un color amarillo intenso.

meaning.en: A bowl with holes used to drain water from food such as pasta or vegetables.
example.en: Drain the pasta in a colander.
example.es: Escurre la pasta en un escurridor.

meaning.en: A tool with a fine mesh used to separate finer particles from larger ones.
example.en: Sift the flour through a fine sieve.
example.es: Tamiza la harina con un tamiz fino.
notes: Normalised from source term: shieve

meaning.en: Happening or occurring often.
example.en: Frequent delays have made passengers angry.
example.es: Los retrasos frecuentes han enfadado a los pasajeros.

meaning.en: A state of not being emotionally involved in something.
example.en: He spoke about the accident with surprising detachment.
example.es: Habló del accidente con un sorprendente distanciamiento emocional.
notes: Emotional-distance sense. Consolidated duplicate source row(s): detachment.

meaning.en: The act or process of separating something from something else.
example.en: The detachment of the panel from the wall caused the alarm to sound.
example.es: El desprendimiento del panel de la pared hizo que sonara la alarma.
notes: Physical-separation sense. Consolidated duplicate source row(s): detachment.

meaning.en: An impressive achievement requiring skill, strength or courage.
example.en: Finishing the race in those conditions was an impressive feat.
example.es: Terminar la carrera en esas condiciones fue una proeza impresionante.
notes: Consolidated duplicate source row(s): feat.

meaning.en: In a deliberately playful, knowing or slightly ironic way.
example.en: “A perfect solution,” he said archly, knowing that it was anything but perfect.
example.es: «Una solución perfecta», dijo con ironía, sabiendo que no lo era en absoluto.

meaning.en: The act of examining an area to obtain information, especially for military or strategic purposes.
example.en: The soldiers carried out reconnaissance before moving into the area.
example.es: Los soldados realizaron un reconocimiento antes de entrar en la zona.
notes: Normalised from source term: recoinnaisance Consolidated duplicate source row(s): reconnaissance.

meaning.en: Cloth or textile material made by weaving, knitting or similar processes.
example.en: The curtains are made from a light cotton fabric.
example.es: Las cortinas están hechas de un tejido ligero de algodón.
notes: Textile sense.

meaning.en: The basic structure or framework of a society, organisation or system.
example.en: Trust is essential to the social fabric of a community.
example.es: La confianza es esencial para el entramado social de una comunidad.
notes: Figurative structure sense.

meaning.en: A limit, condition or measurable factor that defines how something works or is considered.
example.en: We need to define the parameters of the project before we begin.
example.es: Tenemos que definir los parámetros del proyecto antes de empezar.
notes: Headword normalised from “parameters” to lemma “parameter”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: To cross or meet at a point.
example.en: The two roads intersect just outside the village.
example.es: Las dos carreteras se cruzan justo a las afueras del pueblo.
notes: Consolidated duplicate source row(s): intersect.

meaning.es: salpicar; llenar de pequeñas cantidades o ejemplos
meaning.en: To scatter or include many small examples or amounts of something throughout something else.
example.en: The article is peppered with references to popular culture.
example.es: El artículo está salpicado de referencias a la cultura popular.
relations.patterns: pepper something with something; be peppered with + noun
notes: Headword normalised from “peppered” to lemma “pepper”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: Large, flat, high-quality sheets of glass, especially for shop windows.
example.en: The shop window is made of thick plate glass.
example.es: El escaparate está hecho de vidrio plano grueso.

meaning.en: Used at the end of a list to mean that similar things continue.
example.en: We need bread, milk, fruit and so on.
example.es: Necesitamos pan, leche, fruta, etcétera.

meaning.en: To spread over a large area in an untidy or uncontrolled way.
example.en: The city began to sprawl into the surrounding countryside.
example.es: La ciudad empezó a extenderse de forma desordenada hacia el campo de alrededor.

meaning.en: Unable to see.
example.en: The organisation provides guide dogs for blind people.
example.es: La organización proporciona perros guía a personas ciegas.
notes: Literal sight sense.

meaning.es: ajeno a; incapaz o reacio a ver
meaning.en: Unwilling or unable to notice or understand something.
example.en: He seemed blind to the problems his decision had caused.
example.es: Parecía ajeno a los problemas que había causado su decisión.
notes: Figurative awareness sense.

meaning.en: Unusual or impressive enough to deserve attention.
example.en: She made remarkable progress in a very short time.
example.es: Hizo un progreso extraordinario en muy poco tiempo.

meaning.en: A company or person that makes goods, usually in large quantities.
example.en: Car manufacturers are investing heavily in electric vehicles.
example.es: Los fabricantes de automóviles están invirtiendo mucho en vehículos eléctricos.
notes: Normalised from source term: manufactureres Headword normalised from “manufacturers” to lemma “manufacturer”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: A member of a fire service who holds an officer or supervisory role.
example.en: Senior fire officers coordinated the emergency response.
example.es: Los oficiales superiores del servicio de bomberos coordinaron la respuesta de emergencia.
notes: Headword normalised from “fire officers” to lemma “fire officer”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: A person whose job is to extinguish fires and rescue people.
example.en: A firefighter helped the family leave the building safely.
example.es: Un bombero ayudó a la familia a salir del edificio de forma segura.

meaning.es: a quien; a quienes; quien en función de objeto (formal)
meaning.en: The object form of 'who', used especially in formal English.
example.en: The woman whom I spoke to was very helpful.
example.es: La mujer con la que hablé fue muy amable.

meaning.en: A detailed technical drawing showing how a building, machine or other object is to be made.
example.en: The architect showed us the original blueprint of the building.
example.es: El arquitecto nos enseñó el plano técnico original del edificio.
notes: Literal technical-drawing sense.

meaning.en: A detailed plan or model for how something should be developed or achieved.
example.en: The report provides a blueprint for reforming the education system.
example.es: El informe ofrece un plan detallado para reformar el sistema educativo.
relations.collocations: blueprint for reform; blueprint for change
notes: Figurative detailed-plan sense.

meaning.en: To put or leave something in a particular place.
example.en: She deposited the keys on the table.
example.es: Depositó las llaves sobre la mesa.
notes: Physical-placement sense. Headword normalised from “deposited” to lemma “deposit”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: To pay money into a bank account.
example.en: The money was deposited into her account the following day.
example.es: El dinero fue ingresado en su cuenta al día siguiente.
notes: Banking sense. Headword normalised from “deposited” to lemma “deposit”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: A highly secure room used for storing money, valuables or important documents.
example.en: The bank stores valuable documents in a secure vault.
example.es: El banco guarda documentos valiosos en una cámara acorazada.
notes: Secure-room sense.

meaning.en: An arched roof or ceiling, or a chamber with an arched roof.
example.en: The church has a magnificent stone vault above the nave.
example.es: La iglesia tiene una magnífica bóveda de piedra sobre la nave.
notes: Architectural sense.

meaning.en: Having a large amount of money, property or valuable possessions.
example.en: The area has become popular with wealthy buyers.
example.es: La zona se ha vuelto popular entre compradores adinerados.

meaning.en: To calculate or estimate an amount, cost, time or probability.
example.en: Experts reckoned the repairs would cost about ten thousand euros.
example.es: Los expertos calcularon que las reparaciones costarían unos diez mil euros.
relations.patterns: reckon + clause; reckon something at + amount
notes: Estimate/calculate sense. Headword normalised from “reckoned” to lemma “reckon”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: To think or believe something, especially informally.
example.en: I reckon we'll arrive before eight.
example.es: Creo que llegaremos antes de las ocho.
notes: Informal think/believe sense. Headword normalised from “reckoned” to lemma “reckon”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: Approximately; used after a number or amount.
example.en: There were thirty people or so at the meeting.
example.es: Había unas treinta personas, más o menos, en la reunión.

meaning.en: To take something that belongs to someone else without permission.
example.en: He was caught stealing food from the shop.
example.es: Lo sorprendieron robando comida de la tienda.
notes: Headword normalised from “stealing” to lemma “steal”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: Extremely surprising or impressive.
example.en: The view from the top was absolutely astonishing.
example.es: La vista desde la cima era absolutamente asombrosa.

meaning.en: A carefully planned robbery, especially one involving a large amount of money or valuables.
example.en: The film is based on a carefully planned bank heist.
example.es: La película se basa en un atraco a un banco cuidadosamente planificado.

meaning.en: To guide, direct or cause someone or something to go in a particular direction.
example.en: She led the team through a difficult period.
example.es: Dirigió al equipo durante un periodo difícil.
notes: Headword normalised from “led” to lemma “lead”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: To kill someone intentionally and unlawfully.
example.en: The journalist was murdered while investigating the case.
example.es: El periodista fue asesinado mientras investigaba el caso.
notes: Headword normalised from “murdered” to lemma “murder”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: To change the form, structure or character of something.
example.en: The renovation reshaped the entire neighbourhood.
example.es: La renovación transformó por completo el barrio.
notes: Headword normalised from “reshaped” to lemma “reshape”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: To weaken or undermine an established system, authority or idea, often secretly.
example.en: The campaign was designed to subvert public confidence in the institution.
example.es: La campaña estaba diseñada para socavar la confianza pública en la institución.

meaning.en: To depend on someone or something for support, help or success.
example.en: Many small businesses rely on repeat customers.
example.es: Muchas pequeñas empresas dependen de los clientes habituales.

meaning.en: To visit or go to a place often.
example.en: Writers and artists used to frequent this café.
example.es: Escritores y artistas solían frecuentar este café.
notes: Duplicate term retained as a separate source row for review.

meaning.es: travelling cenital; plano cenital en movimiento
meaning.en: A moving camera shot filmed from above while following a subject.
example.en: The director uses an overhead tracking shot to follow the character through the crowd.
example.es: El director utiliza un travelling cenital para seguir al personaje entre la multitud.

meaning.en: A small piece, part or amount of something.
example.en: There were small bits of glass on the floor.
example.es: Había pequeños trozos de cristal en el suelo.
notes: Headword normalised from “bits” to lemma “bit”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: Nearly, but not completely.
example.en: We're almost ready to leave.
example.es: Estamos casi listos para salir.

meaning.en: At or to a lower level or position.
example.en: The temperature fell below zero during the night.
example.es: La temperatura cayó por debajo de cero durante la noche.

meaning.en: Possibly; maybe.
example.en: Perhaps we should try a different approach.
example.es: Quizás deberíamos probar un enfoque diferente.

meaning.es: con el trasfondo de; en el contexto de
meaning.en: In the context of surrounding events, conditions or visual scenery.
example.en: The story takes place against the background of a major political crisis.
example.es: La historia transcurre con el trasfondo de una gran crisis política.
notes: Normalised from source term: the background against

meaning.en: In addition; too.
example.en: She speaks French and also understands Italian.
example.es: Habla francés y también entiende italiano.

meaning.en: Existing or appearing without a physical body or visible source.
example.en: A disembodied voice came from the speaker in the corner.
example.es: Una voz incorpórea salió del altavoz de la esquina.

meaning.en: To disagree with someone verbally, often angrily.
example.en: They often argue about how to spend their money.
example.es: A menudo discuten sobre cómo gastar su dinero.
relations.patterns: argue with someone; argue about/over something
notes: Disagreement sense.

meaning.en: To give reasons supporting or opposing an idea, opinion or proposal.
example.en: The author argues that the current system is unfair.
example.es: El autor sostiene que el sistema actual es injusto.
relations.patterns: argue that + clause; argue for/against + noun
notes: Reasoned-argument sense.

meaning.es: generalizado; omnipresente; que lo impregna todo
meaning.en: Spreading widely throughout an area, group or situation.
example.en: There is a pervasive sense of uncertainty throughout the novel.
example.es: Hay una sensación generalizada de incertidumbre a lo largo de la novela.

meaning.en: A well-known building, place or feature that is easy to recognise.
example.en: The cathedral is one of the city's best-known landmarks.
example.es: La catedral es uno de los lugares emblemáticos más conocidos de la ciudad.
notes: Headword normalised from “landmarks” to lemma “landmark”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.es: a través de; de un lado al otro
meaning.en: From one side or end of something to the other.
example.en: We walked through the forest for nearly two hours.
example.es: Caminamos a través del bosque durante casi dos horas.
notes: Movement/position sense. Normalised from source term: throught

meaning.en: By means of or as a result of something.
example.en: She found the job through a friend.
example.es: Encontró el trabajo por medio de un amigo.
notes: Means/channel sense. Normalised from source term: throught

meaning.en: During the whole of a period of time.
example.en: It rained through the night.
example.es: Llovió durante toda la noche.
notes: Time-period sense. Normalised from source term: throught

meaning.en: In a strange or unusual way.
example.en: Weirdly, nobody seemed surprised by the announcement.
example.es: Curiosamente, nadie pareció sorprendido por el anuncio.

meaning.en: To transport someone or something instantly, especially in science fiction.
example.en: In the series, the crew can beam people up to the spaceship.
example.es: En la serie, la tripulación puede teletransportar a las personas a la nave espacial.
notes: Normalised from source term: beams…up

meaning.en: To interest someone and keep their attention or involvement.
example.en: The opening question immediately engages the reader.
example.es: La pregunta inicial capta de inmediato el interés del lector.

meaning.en: To make a mechanism or part of a machine begin to operate or connect.
example.en: Press the pedal to engage the mechanism.
example.es: Pulsa el pedal para activar el mecanismo.
relations.patterns: engage in + noun/-ing; engage with + noun

meaning.en: To begin fighting or taking military action against an opponent.
example.en: The troops were ordered not to engage the enemy.
example.es: Se ordenó a las tropas que no entablaran combate con el enemigo.
relations.patterns: engage the enemy; engage in combat

meaning.en: Described or named in a knowing, ironic or playfully formal way.
example.en: The building was archly termed a “masterpiece” by one critic.
example.es: Un crítico denominó irónicamente al edificio una «obra maestra».

meaning.en: To grasp the meaning, significance or explanation of something.
example.en: I understood the main idea, but I missed some details.
example.es: Entendí la idea principal, pero se me escaparon algunos detalles.
notes: Headword normalised from “understood” to lemma “understand”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: Not having enough of something; being without it.
example.en: The proposal is lacking in practical detail.
example.es: La propuesta carece de detalles prácticos.

meaning.en: The way a surface or substance feels or looks.
example.en: The sauce has a smooth, creamy texture.
example.es: La salsa tiene una textura suave y cremosa.
relations.collocations: smooth texture; rough texture; creamy texture
notes: Physical surface/consistency sense.

meaning.en: The distinctive quality, complexity or character of something, especially writing, music or experience.
example.en: The novel gains texture from its many different voices.
example.es: La novela gana riqueza y textura gracias a sus distintas voces.
notes: Figurative quality/complexity sense.

meaning.en: Lit from behind so that the subject is outlined or partly silhouetted.
example.en: The actor appears as a dark, backlit silhouette.
example.es: El actor aparece como una silueta oscura iluminada desde atrás.

meaning.en: Signs collectively, especially those giving directions or information.
example.en: Clear signage makes the station easier to navigate.
example.es: Una señalización clara hace que sea más fácil orientarse en la estación.

meaning.en: The places, objects and conditions around a person or thing.
example.en: The hotel is quiet despite its busy surroundings.
example.es: El hotel es tranquilo a pesar del entorno concurrido.

meaning.en: Something that blocks movement, access, communication or progress.
example.en: Language can create barriers between people.
example.es: El idioma puede crear barreras entre las personas.
notes: Headword normalised from “barriers” to lemma “barrier”; original form preserved in source_term.

meaning.en: An act of changing position or moving from one place to another.
example.en: Any sudden move could frighten the animal.
example.es: Cualquier movimiento repentino podría asustar al animal.
notes: Physical-movement sense.

meaning.en: An action taken by a player during a game.
example.en: That was the best move available on the board.
example.es: Esa era la mejor jugada disponible en el tablero.
notes: Game sense.

meaning.en: A deliberate action or decision intended to achieve something.
example.en: Changing careers was a difficult but necessary move.
example.es: Cambiar de profesión fue una decisión difícil pero necesaria.
notes: Deliberate-action/decision sense.

meaning.es: realidad visceral; realidad cruda e inmediata
meaning.en: A reality experienced in an immediate, physical and deeply emotional way.
example.en: The documentary tries to capture the visceral reality of life in the conflict zone.
example.es: El documental intenta captar la realidad visceral de la vida en la zona de conflicto.
